correctness.rationale: Exact proof on dense subsets: composition of strict proximity relations gives positive sums; an outward normed ray plus density proves open-ball inclusion if and only if the center distance is at most the positive difference; all positive integer-combination closed thresholds follow. Irrational arithmetic density recovers the entire metric; surjectivity and completion plus Mazur–Ulam yield affine extension. Rational-scale nonlinear homeomorphism preserves each integer-unit threshold but moves the midpoint. Every boundary and quantifier is handled analytically; finite checker is supplementary only.

originality.rationale: No covering implication was identified. Wang–Tang–Luo (2026) treats one-scale floor-distance preservation and conditional norm-geometric rigidity, whereas the new result uses only two strict threshold predicates and applies across all nonzero real normed spaces, including on dense subsets; the rational ratio counterexample supplies a sharp boundary. Balister et al. (2015) and Balogh–Walters–Zsák (2024) also concern a single step scale. Exact distance preservers assume exact equality of distances, unavailable here. A published two-radius finite metric-frame classification concerns arbitrary metric realizations, not rigidity within normed metrics. Bibliographic novelty remains qualified by unindexed equivalents.

value.rationale: The result exposes a sharp arithmetic transition in a natural metric-recovery problem: two strict binary proximity relations determine all normed-space distances on arbitrary dense subsets exactly when the radius ratio is irrational. It eliminates the genuine nonlinear one-step freedom in spaces with max-summand geometry, has no reflexivity/smoothness/dimension requirements, and clarifies which data from two geometric adjacency graphs suffice. The exact boundary is supported by explicit rational-ratio counterexamples. This reusable structural rigidity lemma is more than a rescaling of a one-step theorem.
